title: Pressing the button to release steam is unnecessarily difficult...
text:
Pressing the button to release steam is unnecessarily difficult.... [[VIDEOID:92802fd7aaa86092f4cb77c6f2a66f96]] We got this AFMAT steamer trough Vine, but we didn't like it at all, and ended up paying for the PurSteam. The main issue is the convoluted trigger button system. With your thumb, you have to slide up a child lock tab, then press down on the button. The tab has lines or grooves on them to help your thumb grip, but it's not enough, you need to push from the bottom edge of the tab where you can get a grip, then press down, but your thumb ends up hurting after awhile. With the Pursteam, the Child lock is a button you push to slide and unlock. Then you no longer have to deal with it. You simply press the trigger on the handle. The AFMAT requires your thumb to press up on the child lock tab at ALL TIMES during use. Hard to articulate, so please watch the video.

Both the AFMAT and the Pursteam provide you with essentially the same accessories, so it boils down to the triggering mechanism. The trigger on the Pursteam is a no brainer winner. Here is a link to the Pursteam: https://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B06XHXFHWG/ref=ppx_yo_dt_b_search_asin_title?ie=UTF8&psc=1

Having said all that, not everyone will struggle with the AFMAT, some can probably grip and slide the child lock tab just fine. For others, it will be a knack that they need to master. It is actually difficult enough already that you have to concentrate on how hard or light to press at your cleaning target, let alone having to do that and at the same time make sure your thumb keeps pressing up on the tab. You see if you get close to an oven knob, you don't want to press too hard, the steam will bounce off the knob, you need to lighten your press. In power tools, I guess this is equivalent to what's called variable speed. The Pursteam's trigger handle makes it so much easier to control this variable speed.

We are subtracting 2 stars for the unnecessarily difficult trigger system.
